To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) there are significant adverse effects on the child of a prolonged deceleration in labor, and 2) there are significant effects of midforceps delivery.
prolonged deceleration of the fetal heart rate is the most important factor in the etiology of cerebral palsy, followed by the type of delivery (forceps versus cesarean section).

the following labor characteristics are associated with long-term adverse effects on the child’s development: prolonged deceleration (more than 2 minutes), secondary arrest of dilation (more than one hour), and arrest of descent (more than one-half hour).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the labor process on the fetus.
the study of the relationship of labor and delivery to the development of the newborn and the long-term effects of these events on the infant.
the effects of labor on the fetus and newborn.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a labor complicated by a prolonged deceleration is associated with a greater risk of a difficult delivery and an adverse effect on the offspring.

a prolonged and abnormal labor, especially when complicated by fetal distress, is associated with a significantly increased incidence of neonatal morbidity and mortality and with a significantly increased risk of neurologic and behavioral abnormalities in the offspring.

the most significant long-term effects on infants of the labor pattern and type of delivery are those of midforceps procedures and those labors with deceleration, arrest of dilatations or descent, or a combination of these.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are significant adverse long-term effects on infants born following a labor characterized by deceleration or arrest of dilatations or descent.

a prolonged labor with a secondary arrest of dilataion or a secondary arrest of descent is associated with a higher incidence of fetal distress, meconium, and a higher incidence of operative delivery.
the long-term effects of the labor pattern and the mode of delivery on the child are related to the degree of fetal distress and to the type of delivery.
